title: Modular Header
description:
The companion to DRX Kits. A custom door opening needs a header as well as rails, so DRX customers still had to order a custom header and wait, or fabricate one themselves. The modular header comes in 48" lengths that installers cut to size and splice together for pairs of doors, so an entire opening can be built with no factory lead time.

We reused existing header extrusion, sourced the splice and drilling jig from an outside vendor, and launched 11 SKUs alongside the kits in April 2025.

brief.label: Problem
brief.text: With DRX, customers were still forced to buy custom headers or work out complicated fabrication themselves.

brief.label: Solution
brief.text: Cut-to-length header channels in 4" and 4-1/2" sizes, with a splice for pairs of doors and a jig that locates closer and pivot preparation.

brief.label: Value
brief.text: Installers save time and labor with a modular system. Temperers no longer wait on CRL manufacturing.

brief.label: Sourcing
brief.text: Headers from existing inventory; splice and jig bought from an outside vendor.

brief.label: Market
brief.text: Glass office market of $500–600M (2021), growing 7–8% a year through 2028.

charts.title: System lineup
charts.caption: Everything an installer needs to build a custom single or double door opening on site.

swot.strengths:
The first system of its kind: custom door rail lengths made in the shop instead of waiting on the manufacturer
The header completes the package, cut to match custom DRX rail lengths
swot.weaknesses:
Slow market acceptance for a new way of installing door rails
DRX costs more than the standard DRS system
swot.opportunities:
Win customers frustrated by lead times
Give glazing contractors and temperers more control over their schedules
swot.threats:
Can be copied by competitors
Cost may outweigh the benefit for some customers
